title: Kidney Tumor Study München Klinik Bogenhausen
summary:
The aim of the study is to examine different surgical procedures for kidney tumors by examining complication rates and survival times.
This study aims to observe complication rates after different kidney operations. The goal here is to continually monitor the operational quality of our center and to draw conclusions about decisions when choosing therapy based on the data collected. The study is being carried out at the Munich Klinik Bogenhausen gGmbH. A total of at least 300 patients should take part in the study.
As part of the study, only data from routine treatment should be recorded and evaluated. This includes, among others, the following data:
 Surgical procedure used (open vs. minimally invasive surgery)
 Expertise of the surgeon
 Hemoglobin content of the blood (parameter about blood loss) before and after surgery
 Creatinine value (parameter about kidney function) before and after surgery
 Duration of the interruption of the blood supply to the kidney during the operation (so-called ischemia time)
 Presence of drainage and timing of removal
 Occurrence of other complications during the operation or the postoperative phase (e.g. bleeding, injury to neighboring organs), which are classified according to the so-called Clavien-Dindo classification
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of kidney, except renal pelvis

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Histopathological evidence of renal cell carcinoma
- Availability of the image data from the cross-sectional imaging (CT or MRI; CD, USB, internal clinic data storage)
- Primary operation in the Department of Urology at the Munich Clinic gGmbH
- Ability to give consent to participate in the study (for legally cared for patients by the legal carer)
Exclusion criteria:
- Known, hereditary or acquired bleeding tendency (participation is possible if there is a medication-related bleeding tendency; the medication will be adjusted according to the recommendation of the initially ordering doctor or the responsible department in the hospital)
- Anatomical anomalies such as severe scoliosis or short stature that prevent a standardized approach
- Patients with urothelial carcinoma of the upper urinary tract (e.g. renal pelvic carcinoma)
